paragraphs.title: The Unification of Israel and David’s Kingship

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron.”
easy.q: Who came to David unto Hebron?

answers: We are thy bone and thy flesh
easy.explanation: They said, “Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.”
easy.q: What did the tribes say to David?

easy.explanation: The elders came to David at Hebron, made a league with him, and anointed him king.
easy.q: Where was David anointed king over Israel?

answers: He had led Israel even when Saul was king
medium.explanation: They remembered that David had led Israel when Saul was king.
medium.q: Why did Israel regard David as a suitable leader?

medium.explanation: The LORD said David would be “a captain over Israel,” meaning a leader.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “captain” mean in this passage?

answers: David was anointed, then the tribes came, then a league was made
The tribes came, a league was made, and David was anointed
David fled, then the elders came, and afterward a league was made
medium.explanation: The tribes came, the elders made a league with David, and they anointed him king.
medium.q: What was the correct order of events?

answers: They entered into an agreed relationship with David
They asked him to leave Israel
challenge.explanation: A league was a formal covenant or agreement between David and the elders.
challenge.q: What does making a league show about David and the elders of Israel?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says, “he reigned forty years.”
challenge.q: How long did David reign altogether?

answers: Thirty-three years in Hebron and seven years in Jerusalem
Seven years and six months in Hebron, and thirty-three years in Jerusalem
The same number of years in both places
challenge.explanation: David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How long did David reign in Hebron and Jerusalem?

paragraphs.title: The Capture of Jerusalem and the Establishment of the City of David

easy.explanation: David and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites.
easy.q: Against whom did David go when he came to Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion.”
The strong hold of Zion became “the city of David.”
easy.q: What name did David give the strong hold?

answers: They appealed to the blind and the lame and said David could not enter
They asked him to make a covenant
medium.explanation: The Jebusites said that David could not come in, mentioning the blind and the lame.
medium.q: What did the Jebusites say to keep David from entering?

medium.explanation: A strong hold is a fortified place, and David captured Zion.
medium.q: What does “strong hold” mean in this passage?

answers: He dwelt in the fort and built round about it
He gave it back to the Jebusites
medium.explanation: David dwelt in the fort, called it the city of David, and built round about it.
medium.q: What did David do after taking the strong hold?

answers: The capture allowed David to establish it as a center bearing his name
The Jebusites gave it that name
The name came from a place near Tyre
challenge.explanation: After taking the strong hold of Zion, David called it the city of David.
challenge.q: What is the connection between taking Zion and calling it the city of David?

answers: To the number of his men alone
To the LORD God of hosts being with him
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “the LORD God of hosts was with him.”
challenge.q: To what does the passage attribute David’s growing success?

answers: The fortress became part of the establishment of David’s rule
The Jebusites became kings of Israel
challenge.explanation: David occupied the fortress, named it after himself, and built around it.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the change from the strong hold of Zion to the city of David?

paragraphs.title: Recognition of the Kingdom and the Building of David’s House

easy.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers, cedar trees, carpenters, and masons.
easy.q: Who sent messengers and building materials to David?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “they built David an house.”
easy.q: What did they build for David?

easy.explanation: The passage says there were yet sons and daughters born to David.
easy.q: What was born to David in Jerusalem?

answers: That the LORD had established him king and exalted his kingdom
That Hiram had become king of Israel
medium.explanation: David perceived that the LORD had established him king and exalted his kingdom.
medium.q: What did David understand after his house and kingdom were established?

answers: The LORD had appointed and secured him as king
The LORD removed him from the throne
David built a house for the LORD
medium.explanation: The wording describes the LORD appointing and firmly setting David as king.
medium.q: What does “established him king” mean in this passage?

answers: For the king of Tyre’s sake
medium.explanation: David understood that the LORD exalted his kingdom “for his people Israel’s sake.”
medium.q: For whose sake did the LORD exalt David’s kingdom?

answers: The materials and craftsmen helped build a house for David
Hiram sent Philistines to fight David
challenge.explanation: Hiram supplied cedar, carpenters, and masons to build David a house.
challenge.q: How did Hiram’s assistance contribute to David’s kingdom?

answers: David’s household was becoming established there
challenge.explanation: The births are presented as part of David’s growing household in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What can be learned from David having additional sons and daughters in Jerusalem?

challenge.explanation: Solomon is listed among those born to David in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Which name appears among David’s children born in Jerusalem?

paragraphs.title: The First Campaign against the Philistines

answers: They heard that David had been anointed king over Israel
David had sent them cedar trees
They wanted to build him a house
easy.explanation: The Philistines came after hearing that David had been anointed king over Israel.
easy.q: Why did the Philistines come up to seek David?

easy.explanation: The passage says they spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
easy.q: Where did the Philistines spread themselves?

easy.explanation: David asked the LORD whether he should go up against the Philistines.
easy.q: What did David do before going to battle?

answers: Go up, for I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand
medium.explanation: The LORD told David to go up and promised to deliver the Philistines into his hand.
medium.q: What was the LORD’s answer to David?

medium.explanation: The Philistines left their images, meaning their idols, behind.
medium.q: What does “images” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: David called the place Baal-perazim because the LORD had broken forth upon his enemies.
medium.q: What name did David give the place where he smote the Philistines?

answers: The name described the LORD breaking forth against David’s enemies
The Philistines gave it the name
challenge.explanation: David said, “The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me.”
challenge.q: Why was the place called Baal-perazim?

answers: They built a house for David
They made a league with Israel’s elders
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “there they left their images.”
challenge.q: What did the Philistines do after they were defeated?

answers: He sought divine direction before military action
He was not king of Israel
He depended only on the Philistine army
challenge.explanation: David asked the LORD for guidance before going up against the Philistines.
challenge.q: What does David’s inquiry of the LORD before battle show?

paragraphs.title: The Second Campaign and the Flanking Victory

answers: They came up again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim
They left the land for Tyre
They built a house in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The Philistines came up yet again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
easy.q: What did the Philistines do in the second campaign?

answers: Fetch a compass behind them and come upon them over against the trees
easy.explanation: The LORD told David not to go up directly, but to circle behind them.
easy.q: What did the LORD command David to do?

easy.explanation: David smote them “from Geba until thou come to Gazer.”
easy.q: How far did David smite the Philistines?

answers: The sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees
medium.explanation: The LORD told David to act when he heard the sound of a going in the tops of the trees.
medium.q: What was the signal to begin the attack?

answers: Trees or a wooded area used as a landmark
medium.explanation: The KJV refers to the tops of the mulberry trees as the place where the signal would be heard.
medium.q: What are “mulberry trees” in this passage?

answers: The LORD commanded him to circle around and attack from behind
medium.explanation: The LORD gave David a different strategy for the second battle.
medium.q: Why did David not attack the Philistines in the same way as before?

answers: The LORD would lead and give David victory
David would fight without an army
The LORD commanded David to retreat
challenge.explanation: The phrase promises that the LORD would go before David to smite the Philistine host.
challenge.q: What does “the LORD go out before thee” mean in this battle?

challenge.explanation: David was commanded to circle behind the Philistines and come upon them over against the trees.
challenge.q: What strategy was used in the second campaign?

answers: He did exactly as the LORD had commanded
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him.”
challenge.q: What did David do after receiving the LORD’s command?
